takeaways: A focus indicator is at least as large as a 2 CSS px thick outline around the unfocused component, and its pixels change by at least 3:1 between unfocused and focused states.
It is Level AAA. At AA, 2.4.7 only asks that focus is visible.
The 3:1 compares the same pixels before and after focus. 1.4.11 compares colors against what is next to them.
A solid 2px outline in a color with 3:1 against the background meets it for most components.
failures: A 1px outline, too thin to meet the size
A subtle tint change on the button background
A thin underline under a large card
check: Measure the ring: is it at least 2px thick all the way around?
Compare the ring color with what those pixels were before focus. Is it 3:1 or more?
Check the ring on every surface the component can sit on.

quiz.question: A button’s focus style is a 1px solid dark blue outline with 8:1 contrast against the white page. Does it meet 2.4.13?
options: Yes. The contrast is well above 3:1
No. Its area is smaller than a 2px perimeter
Yes. Any visible focus style passes
quiz.why: Both parts must pass: size and contrast. A 1px outline covers about half the area of a 2px one, so it is too small however strong the color.

spec: Give the focus ring’s thickness, offset and color for each component.
List the contrast between ring and background on each surface color.
For thin or unusual shapes, such as inline links, show how the indicator is drawn.
review: Is this ring 2px or more all the way around?
What was under the ring before focus, and how much does it change?
Are we aiming for AAA here, or is 2.4.7 the target?
tradeoff: A bold ring can feel heavy in a refined interface. A two-tone ring, a thin light line inside a dark one, meets the size and contrast on any background and can still be tuned to the brand.
system: Define one focus ring token at 2px or more with a tested color, and apply it in every component.
pitch: A thicker, stronger focus ring costs almost nothing and helps everyone who has ever lost track of where they are on a page.
